subject: research/capture-syncedit
professional: a senior researcher in multi-camera audio-based synchronisation and automatic multi-camera editing (the reviewer an ICASSP / ACM Multimedia paper on drift-aware audio sync of user-generated video would get), paired with a broadcast multicam editor. They would check first whether the failure regime is a property of the estimator or of the chosen start offset, whether the audio-to-picture (lip-sync) offset against ITU-R BT.1359 is counted, whether a one-frame jump at a cut is really visible (edit blindness, match-on-action practice), whether 12 seeds support '0%', and whether the work cites drift-aware audio sync (Shrestha et al. 2007; Bryan, Smaragdis & Mysore 2012).

evidence.correctness: Ran `/usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py` in a private copy of capture-syncedit + capture-audiosync + capture-edit (2 m 03 s): results.txt byte-IDENTICAL to the committed file. Independent scripts /tmp/claude-0/scratch/recompute.py, recompute2.py, recompute3.py: (1) plain unweighted time-domain np.correlate on a 12,345-sample delay gives 0.7715625 s, gcc_phat 0.7715626 s (true 0.7715625). (2) Population median of the worst of three |U(-40,40) ppm * U(0,3480 s)| drifts by 200k-draw Monte Carlo: 48.37 ms vs reported 48.4 ms. (3) Poisson event share 1-exp(-rJ): 0.0198 at 40 ms, 0.221 at 0.5 s, matching README's 2% / 22%; reported 0.023 for once mode is consistent. (4) cut_damage hand case (two cuts, errors 0/50/-20 ms, events at 10.03 and 19.99 s): expected visible 1, event 1, jump 60 ms; observed identical. (5) Brute-force Theil-Sen on 12 points with 3 outliers: 30.000 ppm, project 30.000. (6) Once-mode visible share over 30k draws using the real Viterbi cut lists and analytic drift errors: 0.446 (mean jump 40.3 ms) vs the 12-seed 0.496 (40.0 ms): within 12-seed noise, but the headline '50%' is the high side. The arithmetic is right given the model; problems are in design and scope.
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 5 tests (README says 5; `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 5 passed in 0.21 s), run.py reproduces results.txt (README says about 3 minutes; 2 min here), the table matches results.txt row for row. Two Next steps are open and listed honestly. The 'gate on the estimator's confidence' recommendation is advice only, nothing implements or tests it. 3.
evidence.verification: Tests cover cut_damage only (zero error, equal errors, event in jump, one-frame threshold, analytic Poisson share). Four mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: the threshold (syncedit.py:36) and event window (:38) mutants were caught; the once-mode error (:54, est[0]-truth_now -> est[0]-d0_s) and fit-mode error (:57, drop the slope term) both SURVIVED. camera_errors and trial, which produce every headline number, have no test. 2.
evidence.craft: Read src/capture_syncedit/syncedit.py (70 lines), experiments/run.py, tests/test_syncedit.py, and the reused capture_audiosync/sync.py and capture_edit/model.py. Small, clear, reuses sibling code instead of copying it, deterministic seeds. Minor: two RNG families (random.Random for the edit, numpy Generator for sync) seeded from the same int with ad hoc offsets (seed*7919+n_cams, seed+10_000); results.txt prints max_err only to 0.1 ms while the README talks of 0.005 ms. 3.
evidence.claims: Numbers in README and project.json all trace to results.txt. But: '0% of cuts' rests on 36 camera tracks per cell (recompute3: 0 of 36 bad at 2 s/-10 dB; Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound 9.7% per track) with no interval anywhere; '50%' is 0.496 from 12 seeds where the population value is 0.446; 'Failure is large, not small ... hundreds of ms' (README.md:42) is presented as a property of the estimator, but recompute3 shows failed tracks land at 816-878 ms, i.e. about -d0 (0.8 s) plus drift, because Theil-Sen over random peaks returns about zero lag: the magnitude is set by the arbitrary start offset (identical 847.9 ms medians in two different cells are this artefact). Limitations are otherwise candid and the AI-assistance note is present. 2.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: GCC-PHAT (Knapp & Carter 1976), audio-based multi-camera sync of user video (Shrestha, Barbieri & Weda, ACM MM 2007; Kammerl et al. ICASSP 2014), drift-aware landmark cross-correlation sync (Bryan, Smaragdis & Mysore, ICASSP 2012), commercial PluralEyes / NLE multicam audio sync, which resample for drift. None is cited. The new content is small: jump = b - a is algebra, and the SNR threshold is capture-audiosync's own threshold re-expressed per cut. A researcher could build on the code, but would need to redo the failure regime with d0 varied and add lip-sync before the result says anything new. 2.
evidence.domain: Departs from practice in three ways a multicam editor and a sync researcher would hit: (a) a multicam edit plays one master audio track, so camera B's picture is offset by its full error b against the sound for its whole shot; ITU-R BT.1359 puts detectability at about +45 ms audio lead / -125 ms lag, and once-mode worst errors (median 48 ms) already sit there, yet this is not counted (the Limitations sentence names a different offset); (b) a one-frame world-time jump at a cut as 'visible' is assumed against edit-blindness findings (Smith & Henderson 2008) and match-on-action practice where editors routinely overlap or drop frames; (c) 'once' is evaluated only at +10 dB while 'fit' is at <=0 dB, so the two modes are never compared at the same SNR. 2.

defects.what: The failure regime's magnitude (hundreds of ms, 69-98% of cuts, 11-24% event repeats) is set by the arbitrary start offset d0=0.8 s: when GCC-PHAT loses the peak, Theil-Sen over random peaks returns about zero lag, so the error is about -d0 plus drift (failed tracks 816-878 ms; identical 847.9 ms medians in two cells). README.md:42 presents it as a property of the estimator; d0 is never varied.

The offset between a camera's picture and the edit's master audio track (lip-sync, ITU-R BT.1359 about +45/-125 ms) is not counted, though once-mode worst errors (median 48 ms) reach it; the Limitations sentence names a different offset (a camera's audio vs its own picture).
camera_errors and trial, which produce every headline number, have no test: mutants that drop the drift term in once mode or the slope in fit mode both survive.

No prior work cited: GCC-PHAT (Knapp & Carter 1976), audio sync of multi-camera user video (Shrestha et al. 2007; Kammerl et al. 2014), drift-aware sync (Bryan, Smaragdis & Mysore 2012), cut visibility (edit blindness, Smith & Henderson 2008).
12 seeds and no intervals: '0% of cuts' rests on 0 of 36 tracks (95% upper bound 9.7%), and the '50%' headline is 0.496 where the population value is 0.446.
'once' is run only at +10 dB and 'fit' only at <=0 dB, so the two sync modes are never compared under the same conditions.

verdict: A small, clean, exactly reproducible simulation (results.txt byte-identical on rerun; GCC-PHAT, drift median 48.4 ms, Poisson event share and cut_damage all recompute independently). It does not meet the bar: tests cover only the cut-counting step (two of four seeded mutants in the sync-error path survive), the dramatic failure regime is an artefact of the fixed 0.8 s start offset rather than of the estimator, the master-audio lip-sync offset that a multicam editor would check first is not modelled, '0%' and '50%' rest on 12 seeds without intervals, and no prior work on audio-based multicam sync is cited. Worth keeping as a component; the claims need narrowing and d0 needs sweeping before the threshold story stands.
